Unknown Disputed: sources disagree

The Public Domain Project date is repeated by Commons, while DAHR gives a different month for the same matrix. Neither date has been silently selected; no recording ledger or labelled source disc was inspected to settle the discrepancy.

  • 18 October 1929 — Public Domain Project and Commons.
  • 18 March 1929 — DAHR matrix CVE-48936.

Matrix, take, sides
CVE-48936; take 3 is the issued master listed by DAHR; face 6-0755. Documented

DAHR identifies take 3 as master and lists the matching Gramophone face. The transferred disc’s run-out has not been inspected, and the source catalogue does not itself specify a take.

[3] [4]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The Public Domain Project is the transfer source; its catalogue associates the item with the Martin Osterwalder collection. This is not an explicit transfer-engineer or restoration credit.

[3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is identified. Upload and release dates are not treated as transfer dates.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

No restoration, equalisation, noise-reduction or editing procedure is documented for the upstream audio.

[1]
Composition rights
Commons applies PD-old-100 to Verdi’s composition. Documented

The source catalogue gives Verdi’s death year as 1901. This does not determine rights in the 1929 recording.

[1] [3]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons describes first release in 1930; the Public Domain Project identifies Electrola EJ 423, order 6-0755, matrix CVE-48936, and tentatively dates first release to 1930. The 1929 session-day disagreement does not affect the pre-1963 release bound. The source’s worldwide expiry claim and its website’s CC BY-SA notice are not used as a sound-recording licence. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.

  • Public-domain recording worldwide — claim made by the Public Domain Project and reproduced by Commons.
  • US pre-1972 sound-recording law provides a continuing term for a 1929/1930 first publication; no separate US permission is established.
